name: Ranger
summary: This revised version of the Ranger was made to attempt to restore the Ranger’s identity as a slayer-based class, which excels at striking down specific targets in combat. The base Ranger is highly situational, and is plagued by source books adding contrasting features in an attempt to adjust its place in the game - this full redux starts over from the beginning to attempt to create a cohesive, highly adaptable alternative.

multiclassing.title: Multiclassing
paragraphs: The following are the requirements to multiclass into a Ranger.

items.label: Proficiencies Gained
items.value: Light and medium armor, shields, simple and martial weapons, and one Ranger skill.

items.label: Hit Points at Higher Levels
items.value: 1d10 (or 6) + your Constitution modifier per Ranger level after 1st

items.label: Skills
items.value: Choose three skills from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, and Survival

blocks.text: You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

items: (a) two shortswords or (b) two simple melee weapons
(a) a dungeoneer’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack
(a) a longbow and a quiver of 20 arrows or (b) a light revolver with 20 light ammo

blocks.text: Rangers begin at level 1 with 5d4 × 10 (120) gold pieces.

rows.features: Favored Enemy, Proficiency Focus, Terrain Master
Fighting Style Advancement, Nature’s Veil, Tempered Expectations

blocks.text: Choose one type of favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, giants, goblinoids, elementals, fey, fiends, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. If your choice commonly speaks one or more languages, you learn to read, speak and write one of those languages.

When you make an attack against your Favored Enemy, you add a bonus to your attack rolls and add a die to damage rolls against them, referred to as your Favor Bonus and Favor Die respectively. These bonuses are listed on the Ranger class table.
Furthermore, you can add your Favor Bonus to any skill check you make to combat, contest, outwit or track your Favored Enemy.

Each time you gain a Ranger level where you would gain the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can choose an additional Favored Enemy from the list above (learning another language as described). Each time you gain one of these additional types you can choose two types of humanoid races as your Favored Enemy instead (for example, you may choose two from dragonkin, kua hono, human, elf, capy’hado, etc.).
You can choose one of the following options:

items: Choose one skill you are proficient with. When you make a roll using that skill proficiency you can add your proficiency bonus to it a second time as long as you were not already doing so.
You gain proficiency in simple and martial firearms.

blocks.text: You are an expert at dealing with set types of environments. You gain one of the following movement types: climbing or swimming. Your speed for this movement type is equal to your base movement speed.
Your mastery of the elements grants you the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on initiative checks.
If you would be surprised in combat, you can take actions and move normally on your first turn.

blocks.text: Additionally, when you are exploring the wilderness you gain the following benefits:

items: Your travel speed is not reduced by difficult or unforgiving terrain.
If you make a Survival Leading Check related to traveling in the wilderness and you are the check leader, you have advantage on your deciding Survival Check.
You find twice as much food as you normally would when foraging.
You always know which way is North unless magically interfered with.
When moving at a fast pace your passive Perception is not reduced.

blocks.text: At 2nd level you adopt a style of fighting as your speciality. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
You have learned to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells, much as a Druid does.

The Ranger table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Ranger spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell’s level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.
For example, if you know the 1st-level spell animal friendship and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast animal friendship using either slot.

blocks.title: Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher

blocks.text: You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the Ranger spell list.

The Spells Known column of the Ranger table shows when you learn more Ranger spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 5th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level. Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the Ranger spells you know and replace it with another spell from the Ranger spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Ranger spells, since your magic draws on your attunement to nature. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a Ranger spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Unless otherwise stated, these calculations are used for your other class and subclass save DCs and spell attacks.
You choose a Ranger archetype, from which you draw your particular hunting and combat techniques. You gain features from your archetype now at 3rd level as a Ranger, then again at 7th, 11th and 15th.
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2 or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1.
You can make two attacks instead of one when you take the Attack action on your turn.

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack you can mark them as your Favored Target for 1 minute, allowing you to treat them as if they were one of your Favored Enemies. You can only have one Favored Target at a time - marking a new one removes the previous mark - but you can use this feature a number of times per Long Rest equal to your proficiency bonus.
Your movement speed increases by 10 feet.
When you score a critical hit against any creature you can roll your Favor Die and add the result to the damage roll. You score a critical hit on a d20 result of 19 or 20.

When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points on your turn, you can immediately move up to your movement speed and make a weapon attack with advantage against another creature in range. You can use this feature a number of times per Long Rest equal to your Favor Bonus.
Your specialized skills sharpen. You may advance one of your Fighting Styles.

As a bonus action on your turn you become magically invisible along with any equipment you are carrying, until the start of your next turn. You can do so a number of times equal to your Favor Bonus per Short or Long Rest.

You have devised methods of combat that exploit an enemy’s unfamiliarity with your tactics. During the first round of combat you can treat all creatures as if they were your Favored Enemies, allowing you to apply all bonuses and features that would entail to them.
You can take the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Additionally, you cannot be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.
You have blindsight out to 30 feet, allowing you to see invisible creatures as if they were plainly visible unless they have otherwise hidden themselves from you. You cannot be blinded or deafened.
You have advantage on saving throws made against the spells and abilities of your Favored Enemies.

When you begin your first turn in combat you can target up to three creatures you can see or are aware of with your Favored Target feature, costing one use of it. Using your Favored Target again does not remove your current targets, and instead adds them to your current Favored Targets.

lore_sections.title: The Ranger
paragraphs: The revised Ranger fills the same roles and aesthetic purposes as the original Ranger class. The Ranger has seen alterations and tweaks across the many core 5th Edition supplements, resulting in a class that is comprised almost entirely of optional features. The Ranger class presented below is meant to be taken as a stand-alone alternative, which outfits the Ranger with more options in combat, emphasizes targeting specific enemy types, and allowing their specific “slayer”-based mechanics to briefly apply to general enemies so they don’t feel entirely out of place in combat that doesn’t feature their specific favored enemies.
This class attempts to evoke a swift combatant who can take action quickly, is prepared for surprise, and strikes down foes with tactical precision. They are adaptable and difficult to pin down.

Several new subclasses are presented with this new iteration of the class, but a GM might review existing Ranger subclasses and incorporate them into this version. Some things may need to be changed to make them work, but the subclass structure is left largely the same to accommodate old subclasses.
